newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Sparks sees lower Argentine wheat, maize sowing.
newsitem.headline: Sparks sees lower Argentine wheat, maize sowing.

text.p: Sparks sees Argentina's area sown with wheat in the 1997/98 season falling 10 percent versus 1996/97, and the area sown with maize falling 7.0 percent, a Sparks South America official said Monday.

Sparks' Vice-president Juan Martin Rebolini said the fall in sown area should lead to 1997/98 Argentine wheat production of 12.7-13.3 million tonnes "in normal conditions." Maize exports, which should be about 10 million tonnes this season, would fall to about 7.5-8 million next season, he said.

Brazilian imports of wheat from all origins should rise next year to 5.8 million tonnes, from five million tonnes this season, said Rebolini, of the local office of U.S. agricultural consultant Sparks Companies of Memphis, Tenn.

Rebolini said world wheat output will rise steadily over the next few years, but that prices will rise faster, reaching about $235 FOB Gulf of Mexico by 2005. Maize prices should reach $180 by the same date, although world production will rise to about 670 million tonnes.
